chains.title: Tentative FLI1-dependent enhancer effect on UTP25
chains.cell_type: Craniofacial developmental cells; activity and FLI1 occupancy in this context are not established

links.claim: FLI1 is a tentative ETS-family candidate. Its QBiC-SELEX entry predicts stronger binding to G, but the best-scoring result uses an ETV5-mapped model and does not show FLI1 occupancy at this site. The shared ETS-family result does not distinguish FLI1 from other candidates.
The variant lies in the enhancer-like cCRE EH38E2863563; its reported activity maxima are not specific to craniofacial developmental cells.

UTP25 is a candidate target because it is nearby and has the highest reported best L2G score across the listed sets. The UTP25–cleft gene score and broad enhancer literature add plausibility, but do not show that this variant regulates UTP25.
Craniofacial developmental cells are a plausible context for the trait, but the evidence does not demonstrate FLI1 occupancy, element activity, or UTP25 regulation in those cells.
The variant is associated with orofacial clefts, but this does not establish a cleft-lip-specific causal effect or that altered UTP25 regulation mediates the association.

predictions: If this chain is correct, FLI1 should occupy the element in relevant cells and show greater binding to G. The variant should produce an FLI1-dependent change in UTP25 regulation; the direction of the expression change cannot be inferred from the binding prediction.
falsified_if: Relevant-cell assays show no FLI1 occupancy, or precise allele editing shows no FLI1-dependent effect on UTP25.

The shared ETS-family prediction does not distinguish ETV3 from the other candidates.
The variant lies in the enhancer-like cCRE EH38E2863563; the reported activity scores are maxima across biosamples, not evidence of activity in craniofacial cells.

IRF6 is a candidate target based on proximity and L2G results, but the supplied evidence does not establish that this variant's cCRE regulates IRF6. The literature search found no variant-specific result linking this site to IRF6.
Craniofacial developmental cells are a plausible context for the cleft association, but this element's activity and ETV3 occupancy in those cells are not demonstrated.
The variant has a reported orofacial-cleft association; the evidence does not establish a cleft-lip-specific causal effect or an ETV3–IRF6 mechanism.

predictions: If this chain is correct, ETV3 should occupy the element in relevant cells, with greater binding to G, and an allele-dependent effect on IRF6 regulation should depend on ETV3.
falsified_if: Relevant-cell assays show no ETV3 occupancy or no reproducible ETV3-dependent allele effect on IRF6.

The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only.
